title: Probability of selecting outside a coordinate set
statement: Let $m$ be a natural number and let $J$ be a set of coordinates among the first $m+2^m$ positions. Choose uniformly a sign vector on these positions, use its first $m$ signs to select one of the $2^m$ data positions, and let the selected coordinate be the corresponding data coordinate. The probability that this coordinate lies outside $J$ equals the number of data positions outside $J$, divided by $2^m$.
hypotheses_covered: $J$ is a finite set of coordinates among the first $m+2^m$ positions
